_comment: F7 — the alert text, written once and never at runtime. Everything here is shipped to
the app verbatim inside data/derived/notifications.json, so what a test renders is what a
phone would show. The pipeline (pipeline/derive/notifications.py) and the browser
(app/src/lib/notify.ts) both fill the same placeholders, and the parity test compares the
Placeholders are exactly the set asserted by pipeline/tests/test_notifications.py:
{street}    the modelled street name, or a fallback for the 210 unnamed segments
{stage}     the street's own flood threshold in feet
{river}     the gauge stage at the hour the message is sent
{category}  the official NWS category at that hour — in the language of the message
{hours}     whole hours from the send to the modelled crossing
{when}      the local crossing time, language-formatted, 12-hour in both languages so
the two messages carry the same digits
Both languages must carry the SAME digits: a Spanish alert that says 48 where the English
says 45 is the failure mode this file exists to make untestable. Do not translate numbers,
street names, 'BrazosCast', or the 12-inch line (see the note on units below).
_units_note: The 12-inch line is quoted in inches in both languages, with the metric equivalent only in
the Spanish guidance that is NOT part of the SMS — a translated 30 cm would break the
digit-parity gate for a reason that has nothing to do with the alert being wrong.

purpose.en: leave while it is still a choice

en.early: BrazosCast 3 days out: the Brazos at Richmond is at {river} ft, {category}. {street} is modelled to go under at {stage} ft — about {hours} h from now, {when}. Plan a dry route and move what you can. This is a model, not an order.
en.soon: BrazosCast 24 h out: {street} is modelled to flood at {stage} ft in about {hours} h ({when}). The river is at {river} ft, {category}. Fuel the car, pack medicines and documents, and tell someone your plan. Do not drive through water.
en.now: BrazosCast 6 h out: water is expected on {street} at {stage} ft by {when}, about {hours} h. The river is at {river} ft, {category}. Leave now if you can, by a route you know is dry. 12 inches of moving water carries most cars away.

es.early: BrazosCast 3 días antes: el Brazos en Richmond está en {river} pies, {category}. Se prevé que {street} quede bajo el agua a {stage} pies: unas {hours} h desde ahora, {when}. Planifique una ruta seca y mueva lo que pueda. Es un modelo, no una orden.
es.soon: BrazosCast 24 h antes: se prevé que {street} se inunde a {stage} pies en unas {hours} h ({when}). El río está en {river} pies, {category}. Cargue gasolina, prepare medicamentos y documentos, y avise su plan a alguien. No conduzca por el agua.
es.now: BrazosCast 6 h antes: se espera agua en {street} a {stage} pies para {when}, unas {hours} h. El río está en {river} pies, {category}. Salga ahora si puede, por una ruta que sepa seca. 12 pulgadas de agua en movimiento arrastran la mayoría de los autos.

en.title: The alert you would get
en.note: simulated send · nothing leaves this page
en.lead: Each message is timed from this street's own modelled crossing, not from the river's category: the official flood stages arrived 7 and 4 hours apart in 2017, which would be three texts in one night and none about this street.
en.quiet: 22:00–07:00 local: the first two are held to 07:00; the 6-hour alert is never held. A held message that would land after the water is dropped, not sent late.
en.none: No crossing is modelled in this forecast, so no alert would be sent.
en.pick: Pick a street to see the message it would produce.
en.short: One message is not shown: it would have landed after the water, and the policy drops it rather than send it late.

es.title: La alerta que recibiría
es.note: envío simulado · nada sale de esta página
es.lead: Cada mensaje se mide desde el cruce modelado de esta calle, no desde la categoría del río: las etapas oficiales de inundación llegaron con 7 y 4 horas de diferencia en 2017, es decir tres mensajes en una noche y ninguno sobre esta calle.
es.quiet: 22:00–07:00 hora local: los dos primeros se retienen hasta las 07:00; la alerta de 6 horas nunca se retiene. Un mensaje retenido que llegaría después del agua se descarta, no se envía tarde.
es.none: No se prevé ningún cruce en este pronóstico, así que no se enviaría ninguna alerta.
es.past: ya enviado, antes de este pronóstico
es.pick: Elija una calle para ver el mensaje que produciría.
es.short: Un mensaje no se muestra: habría llegado después del agua, y la política lo descarta en lugar de enviarlo tarde.
